vectors.title: Transaction frames, addressing and filtering
vectors.applicability: Required within the selected draft profile; exceptions require a prospective versioned rule.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
steps: Submit the pinned raw and Extended Format transaction fixtures, separately and interleaved, to the fabric ingress.
Subscribe delivery edges to all shard groups, to a shard subset, to selected subtrees, and through source-specific and any-source joins.
Announce subtree groups with BRC-127 frames and re-emit frames through an egress bridge onto another group scope.
Corrupt the transaction identifier of a declared share of frames, and run several edges against a shared deduplication cache.
expected: Every edge subscribed to a transaction's BRC-129 group and subtree delivers it; an edge outside them does not.
Raw (BRC-124) and Extended Format (BRC-128) payloads arrive unchanged, alone or interleaved, with no malformed-frame drops.
An edge that verifies payload hashes forwards only frames whose payload hashes to the frame's transaction identifier.
An edge that learns its subtrees from BRC-127 announcements forwards them without static configuration, and an edge on the re-mapped scope receives the bridged frames.
Edges sharing a deduplication cache forward each transaction identifier once; without the cache they keep forwarding, and they resume deduplication after its failover.
Source-specific join and leave take effect, and an any-source configuration is unchanged by the source-specific path.
blockers: Independent oracle for each assertion; retained runs use the harness's own scenario checks
Base image pinned by digest in a retained run

vectors.title: Fragmentation and reassembly
vectors.applicability: Required within the selected draft profile; exceptions require a prospective versioned rule.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
steps: Set the ingress fragmentation MTU below the payload size and submit the pinned transaction fixtures.
Apply declared fragment loss on the edge segment.
expected: Edges reassemble every frame with none abandoned, and each reassembled payload hashes to the frame's transaction identifier.
Shard and subtree filters apply to reassembled frames.
A frame missing a fragment is abandoned at the reassembly bound and never delivered in part.
blockers: Independent oracle for each assertion; retained runs use the harness's own scenario checks

vectors.title: Gap detection and repair
vectors.applicability: Required within the selected draft profile; exceptions require a prospective versioned rule.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
steps: Apply declared loss on the edge segment and inject sequence gaps at the ingress.
Empty the cache of declared retransmission endpoints, and apply per-address, per-chain and per-group rate limits.
Repeat with repair fed by a listener tee without a group join, with NACK proxying across domains, and between fabrics.
expected: Edges detect each gap from the per-flow sequence number and send BRC-126 NACKs; retransmission fills recoverable gaps, including those of Extended Format payloads.
An endpoint without the frame answers MISS, edges escalate by tier to an endpoint that holds it, and a gap that stays open is reported as unrecovered.
Frames sent equal frames delivered plus frames reported unrecovered.
Under rate limits, repair is throttled and acknowledgments continue.
evidence: gap, NACK, ACK, MISS and unrecovered counters
blockers: Independent oracle for each assertion; retained runs use the harness's own scenario checks
Base image pinned by digest in a retained run

expected: Every subscribed edge receives each block announcement and anchor on the block broadcast group, whatever its shard and subtree filters.

vectors.title: BEEF object plane
vectors.applicability: Required within the selected draft profile; exceptions require a prospective versioned rule.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
steps: Submit BEEF submission records (BRC-149) on the open transaction path and on the dedicated BEEF lane, including the BRC-62 specification example and a record naming several topics.
Run transaction and BEEF traffic together through one ingress and one edge set.
Apply declared frame and fragment loss, with multicast and unicast repair.
expected: Edges deliver each object verbatim with a verified content identifier, and an edge electing one encoding version forwards only that version.
Objects larger than the MTU travel as BRC-130 fragments, are reassembled before filtering, and recover at fragment granularity over multicast and unicast repair.
A record naming several topics travels as one frame, keyed by its first topic.
Transaction and BEEF traffic both deliver in full without perturbing each other's sequencing, and per-domain manifests adopt the plane's shard bits independently.

vectors.title: Processor objects and proofs through the fabric
vectors.applicability: Required within the selected draft profile; exceptions require a prospective versioned rule.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
steps: Mine a block containing the fixture transaction.
Observe the processor bridge, the proof bridge, Merkle Service and the header store until Broadcaster reports the transaction mined.
expected: The processor bridge publishes the block's subtree (BRC-143) and block (BRC-144) objects with identities equal to the processor's, and they arrive on the proof bridge's lanes.
Merkle Service fetches the objects from the proof bridge and receives no libp2p announcement.
Broadcaster receives a mined proof whose independently computed root equals the merkle root of the processor's header.
The header store holds the block under the hash of the header-lane bytes, with the processor's merkle root.
evidence: subtree and block bytes from the proof bridge and the processor
blockers: Independent oracle for each assertion; retained runs use the fabric publisher's own checks

Retransmission endpoint fed upstream of the declared impairment
steps: Apply the declared loss between the fabric and the delivery edge, leaving the retransmission feed and every delivery lane unimpaired.

expected: The delivery edge detects every gap and either repairs it or reports it unrecovered; frames sent equal frames delivered plus frames reported unrecovered.

No transaction produces a second financial effect.

vectors.title: Overlay delivery between engines
vectors.applicability: Required within the selected draft profile; exceptions require a prospective versioned rule.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
steps: Submit the pinned Atomic BEEF fixture to the publishing overlay host for the fixture topic.
Repeat the same submission.
expected: Before the submission, the receiving engine holds no output for the fixture.
The publishing host answers with the topic-keyed admittance of BRC-22, and its bridge publishes the record on the BEEF object plane.
The receiving bridge takes the record from its BEEF lane and submits it, and the receiving engine admits it on the topic.
Lookups on both hosts return the output, and each returned BEEF resolves to the submitted transaction.

The repeated submission creates no second admission: each host still holds exactly one output for the fixture. BRC-22 does not define the answer to a repeat, so an empty admittance and the first admittance replayed are both accepted.
blockers: Independent oracle for each assertion; retained runs use the fabric publisher's own checks
The library's own BRC-22 route wraps its answer (V012 brc22.response.topic-keyed), so the retained run's hosts serve BRC-22 and BRC-24 themselves in front of the unmodified engine

vectors.title: BRC-22 submission boundary
vectors.applicability: Required for overlay bridges that submit through BRC-22 and for the engines that receive them; open-interpretation cases are held out of scoring.
preconditions: Digest-locked admitted SUT and dependency closure
Server under test in front of a recording engine
Pinned BRC-22 submit boundary vector file
steps: Send each header vector of the BRC-22 submit boundary vector file to the server under test with a one-byte body.
Read each response body with the client under test.
expected: Standard cases produce the expected topics, rejections and topic-keyed admittance of BRC-22.
Extension cases are recorded as supported or not supported, never as failures.
Open-interpretation cases are recorded without a verdict.
blockers: Laboratory interpretation of the open-interpretation cases
Runtime observations of overlay-express
